key_insight: In life sciences, acceptance of machine learning is shaped not only by perceived usefulness and ease of use, but also by credibility cues like journal impact factor and by perceptions of technology hype.
clinical_relevance: Understanding these acceptance drivers may help research and healthcare organisations improve adoption of ML tools in evidence-based workflows, without assuming enthusiasm alone will drive implementation.
method: Cross-sectional survey of 213 biomedical and life science professionals
Participants drawn from EMEA, LATAM, and North America
Extended TAM tested with PLS-SEM and external variables
evidence_signal: The abstract reports survey-based model testing across 213 professionals using PLS-SEM to examine ML acceptance factors.
watch_item: Findings are based on self-reported, cross-sectional data, so they show association rather than causation and may not generalise to all healthcare settings.
paper_title: Technology acceptance of machine learning in life sciences: the role of hype perception and journal impact factor.
